video_caption: The video segment opens with a static shot of a woman with long dark hair and glasses, wearing a dark blue shirt with a floral pattern. She stands in an indoor setting, with a large, vibrant green leafy plant positioned prominently to her left, and a lighter-colored wall with visible stairs in the background. Starting at the 0:05 mark, white text overlays appear on the screen, introducing the woman. The first line reads "HABLAMOS CON LA DR. CHERRY NG" (WE TALK TO DR. CHERRY NG). This is followed by "Astrónoma en el Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (CNRS) de Francia" (Astronomer at the National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS) of France). Subsequent text reveals her additional roles: "Co-presidenta del grupo de ciencia Cradle of Life del Observatorio del SKA (SKAO)" (Co-chair of the Cradle of Life science working group of the SKA Observatory (SKAO)), and "Y reconocida experta en temas de búsqueda de inteligencia extraterrestre (SETI)" (And recognized expert in topics of search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI)). The woman maintains a calm and slightly smiling expression throughout the text overlay, occasionally blinking, as the camera remains fixed on her.

The video begins with a medium shot of a woman with dark hair and glasses, wearing a dark blue shirt with a white floral pattern, speaking directly to the camera. She smiles and uses hand gestures as she talks, standing in an indoor setting with several large green potted plants in the background, one on the left and another behind her to the right. A staircase with a glass railing is visible in the upper right background. From 00:22, the scene transitions to an animation featuring a rotating grey globe with continents clearly visible, encircled by a network of white lines connecting various points across its surface. The text "SKAO" is displayed in white at the top center of the screen. The animation then zooms out, and the globe appears smaller in the center as a dark, grid-like pattern expands around it. This grid becomes populated with small, glowing, colorful squares that form a vibrant, winding, galaxy-like structure of red, orange, and yellow hues, stretching across the dark, star-filled background. The "SKAO" text remains at the top, and Spanish text overlay reads, "Es un proyecto multinacional que realmente une al mundo para construir algo que hará avanzar nuestro conocimiento del universo." (It is a multinational project that really unites the world to build something that will advance our knowledge of the universe.)

The video opens with a woman with long dark hair and glasses, wearing a multi-colored patterned shirt (dark blue, white, red, and brown patterns), speaking directly to the camera and occasionally gesturing with her right hand. She is positioned indoors in front of large potted plants with green foliage, with a glass staircase or railing visible in the upper right background. Spanish subtitles appear at the bottom: "Así que cuando el SKAO contactó conmigo para copresidir el grupo de trabajo Cradle of Life en 2022 no dudé y acepté inmediatamente. En 2023, también fui invitada a unirme al Comité Asesor de Ciencia e Ingeniería (SEAC) de SKAO. Nos reunimos unas tres veces al año para oír hablar del progreso del SKAO y damos nuestras recomendaciones como expertos sobre este progreso." (Translation: "So when the SKAO contacted me to co-chair the Cradle of Life working group in 2022, I did not hesitate and accepted immediately. In 2023, I was also invited to join the Science and Engineering Advisory Committee (SEAC) for the SKAO, where we meet about three times a year, and we hear about the progress of the SKAO, and we provide our expert recommendations on the progress."). At 0:28, the scene transitions to a dark screen with white text that reads: "Los objetivos del grupo de ciencia Cradle of Life (SKAO)" (Translation: "The objectives of the Cradle of Life science group (SKAO)"). Three small green dots animate beneath the text, appearing sequentially and then fading out.

The segment begins with a woman, wearing glasses and a patterned shirt, speaking directly to the camera from an indoor setting with lush potted plants and a staircase in the background. As she speaks, Spanish subtitles appear, stating: "está interesado en la búsqueda de los orígenes de la vida. Y esto es un tema muy amplio." (is interested in the search for the origins of life. And this is a very broad topic.) The scene then transitions to an animation of a protoplanetary disk, a swirling red-orange cloud of gas and dust with a bright central star, with the text "ESO/L. Calçada, ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO)/Benisty et al." on screen, and Spanish subtitles reading: "Incluye temas como la formación planetaria." (It includes topics such as planetary formation.) This is followed by an animation of Earth rotating in space against a backdrop of stars, displaying the text "ESO/L. Calçada/M. Kornmesser/spaceengine.org" and the Spanish subtitles: "Por ejemplo, la Tierra, cómo se formó y cómo emergió la vida en ella," (For example, Earth, how it was formed and how life emerged on it,). The video then shows another animation of a star surrounded by concentric rings of gas and dust, similar to a protoplanetary disk, with a small inset on the right showing molecular structures, under the text "ESO/M. Kornmesser" and Spanish subtitles: "o temas como la física y la química de las estrellas jóvenes," (or topics like the physics and chemistry of young stars,). Finally, the scene returns to the woman, who continues to speak and gesture with her hands, with Spanish subtitles adding: "así como la búsqueda de inteligencia extraterrestre en algún otro lugar del universo. Así, este grupo de trabajo científico Cradle of Life, lo veo como una plataforma para facilitar todo este tipo de colaboraciones." (as well as the search for extraterrestrial intelligence elsewhere in the universe. Thus, this scientific working group Cradle of Life, I see it as a platform to facilitate all these types of collaborations.)

The video opens with a woman, wearing a patterned button-up shirt and black-rimmed glasses, speaking directly to the camera in an indoor setting with green plants and a staircase in the background. A Spanish caption reads "Hace unos diez años se comenzó la preparación del Libro Blanco de SKA, y esa era la principal actividad del grupo de trabajo por aquel entonces." (About ten years ago, the preparation of the SKA White Paper began, and that was the main activity of the working group at that time). The scene transitions to an aerial view of a vast, reddish-brown desert with circular arrays of white antenna bases and connecting white lines on the ground, with the "SKAO" logo in the top center. The caption changes to "Está tranquilo ahora mismo, pero es porque SKAO está empezando a construirse. Se está progresando mucho." (It's quiet right now, but that's because SKAO is starting to be built. A lot of progress is being made.). This is followed by a shot of a large, partially constructed radio telescope dish being lifted by a crane in the desert under a blue sky, with workers visible near the base. The woman reappears, continuing her speech with the caption "Y creo que el grupo va a jugar de nuevo un papel fundamental, siendo un lugar donde los científicos se prepararán para el día en el que el SKAO esté disponible. En un futuro muy cercano." (And I believe that the group will once again play a fundamental role, being a place where scientists will prepare themselves for the day when the SKAO is available. In the very near future.). The screen then turns dark, displaying white text: "Búsqueda de inteligencia extraterrestre (SETI)" (Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (SETI)), with small green dots animating below. The video concludes with the woman back on screen, stating, "Uno de mis intereses de investigación es SETI. ¿Y qué es eso?" (One of my research interests is SETI. And what is that?).

The video segment opens with a young East Asian woman, wearing black glasses and a dark blue patterned button-up shirt, speaking directly to the camera while gesturing with her right hand. She is positioned indoors, with lush green plants behind her and a blurry architectural background suggesting a modern building or lobby. Spanish subtitles at the bottom read, "Buscamos tecnomarcadores, que son señales avanzadas de tecnología" (We look for technomarkers, which are advanced technology signals), which she is speaking in English. The scene then transitions to an animated cosmic view featuring a bright, yellowish-orange star-like object radiating light through an orange haze, with "SKAO" displayed in the top left corner. A light blue rectangular graphic box appears on the right, initially empty, then illustrating a molecular structure with colored spheres and labels like 'N' and 'R', followed by a yellow spectral line graph. The Spanish subtitle changes to "Es análogo al estudio de biomarcadores," (It is analogous to the study of biomarkers,). The video then cuts to another space animation, showing a dark blue planet silhouetted against a radiant, warm-colored nebula or star, with "ESA/Hubble, M. Kornmesser" attributed in the top right. A transparent rectangular overlay with a spectral graph appears over the planet, displaying various colored peaks. Text labels appear beneath the graph, listing elements like "[Water]", "[Methane]", "[Helium]" on the left, and "[Hydrogen]", "[Ammonia]", "[Oxygen]" on the right, with "Hydrogen" briefly highlighted in green, illustrating the search for molecular lines as the Spanish subtitle reads "donde buscamos líneas moleculares, como la del agua, que pueden ser un indicativo de vida." (where we look for molecular lines, such as water, which can be an indication of life.)

In this video segment, a woman with dark hair, wearing glasses and a dark patterned shirt, speaks directly to the camera in an indoor setting. Behind her are lush green plants and a glimpse of a staircase with a glass railing. On-screen text appears in Spanish, initially stating: "SETI, como una comunidad, ha crecido mucho en los últimos años. Gracias al apoyo de donantes privados." (SETI, as a community, has grown a lot in recent years. Thanks to the support of private donors.) She continues, with accompanying text: "Y uno de los principales ejemplos es la fundación Breakthrough Listen. Es un programa de diez años y 100 millones de dólares dedicado a la búsqueda de inteligencia extraterrestre." (And one of the main examples is the Breakthrough Listen foundation. It is a ten-year, 100 million dollar program dedicated to the search for extraterrestrial intelligence.) The video then transitions to a graphic on a dark blue background, featuring a white city skyline, a full moon, a satellite, and several radio telescope silhouettes, with the text "BREAKTHROUGH LISTEN" and "El objetivo principal de Breakthrough Listen es estudiar un centenar de galaxias cercanas," (The main goal of Breakthrough Listen is to study a hundred nearby galaxies,). This is followed by a stunning image of the Milky Way galaxy with text overlay "monitorizar el plano galáctico" (monitor the galactic plane) and credit "DECaPS2/DOE/FNAL/DECam/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA". The scene then cuts to a dense field of sparkling stars, overlaid with "analizar datos de las mil millones de estrellas más cercanas," (analyze data from the nearest billion stars,) and credit "Matthew Penny (Louisiana State University)". The video returns to the woman, who continues to speak, with the text "Breakthrough Listen ha brindado muchas oportunidades para financiar que los jóvenes se incorporen al campo, y que contribuyan en su investigación, además de apoyar programas de observación en muchos de los radiotelescopios más sensibles del mundo, incluyendo Parkes en Australia, Green Bank en Estados Unidos, el Very Large Array, así como Meerkat en Sudáfrica." (Breakthrough Listen has provided many opportunities to fund young people to join the field, and to contribute to its research, as well as to support observation programs on many of the most sensitive radio telescopes in the world, including Parkes in Australia, Green Bank in the United States, the Very Large Array, as well as Meerkat in South Africa.) Finally, the video transitions to a black screen with white text that reads "La búsqueda de tecnomarcadores" (The search for technosignatures), with three small green dots animating beneath it.

The video opens with a woman with dark hair pulled back, wearing black-framed glasses and a patterned dark blue shirt, speaking directly to the camera with a slight smile. Behind her, a lush green plant stands in an indoor setting with light-colored walls and a hint of a staircase. Spanish text overlays the bottom of the screen: "La forma en la que buscamos tecnomarcadores?" (The way we search for technosignatures?). The scene then transitions to a striking animated depiction of a large, white radio telescope dish against a deep red, fiery cosmic background with glowing nebulae and a bright star in the upper left. The abbreviation "SKAO" is visible in white at the top left, and the text "La mayoría del trabajo se ha realizado en el espectro de radio." (Most of the work has been done in the radio spectrum.) appears at the bottom. This quickly changes back to the woman, who continues to speak, shifting her expression from a gentle smile to a more serious, contemplative look. As she explains, she uses hand gestures to emphasize points, such as opening and closing her hands. The Spanish subtitles continue to appear, explaining the advantages of radio signals for detecting extraterrestrial life: "Y por qué?" (And why?), "Es porque la emisión en radio es relativamente barata de producir" (It's because radio emission is relatively cheap to produce), "Solo hace falta vernos." (Just look at us.), "Como tecnología humana, llevamos décadas usando radiotelecomunicaciones." (As human technology, we've been using radiotelecommunications for decades.), "Así que podríamos esperar que civilizaciones extraterrestres hicieran lo mismo." (So we might expect extraterrestrial civilizations to do the same.), "La emisión de radio es también de las pocas que puede atravesar la atmósfera," (Radio emission is also one of the few that can pass through the atmosphere,), and finally, "lo que significa que fácilmente podemos detectarla desde Tierra, sin tener que mandar al espacio un satélite, un detector, que cuesta más dinero." (which means we can easily detect it from Earth, without having to send a satellite, a detector, into space, which costs more money.). The background remains the same indoor setting with green plants throughout her explanation.

A woman with dark hair and black-framed glasses, wearing a dark blue patterned shirt, speaks directly to the camera. She gestures with her right hand, bringing her thumb and forefinger close together to emphasize a point. In the background, there are lush green potted plants and the interior of what appears to be a modern building with light walls and a glimpse of a staircase. Spanish subtitles at the bottom of the screen read, "Creemos que las señales más probables de detectar son señales variables de banda estrecha." (English: "We believe that the most probable signals to detect are narrow-band variable signals.")

A woman with dark hair and glasses, wearing a dark patterned shirt, speaks directly to the camera from 0:03 to 0:09. She smiles and gestures with her hands, holding them near her chest and moving them slightly to emphasize her words. In the background, lush green plants, including a large leafy bush and a palm-like plant, are visible, suggesting an indoor, possibly atrium-like setting, with a light-colored wall to her left and a staircase to her right. Subtitles appear at the bottom of the screen; the English translation reads: "be dreading of this thing called RFI, which is radio frequency, interference. These are signals generated by human technology such as phones or televisions or satellites," while the Spanish text states: "Si hablas con cualquier radioastrónomo, te dirá que siente pavor ante algo llamado RFI, la interferencia de radiofrecuencia. Se trata de señales generadas por la tecnología humana" (If you talk to any radio astronomer, they will tell you that they are terrified of something called RFI, radio frequency interference. These are signals generated by human technology).

The video opens with a night shot of a large radio telescope dish under a starry sky, with the text "ESO, IRAM, ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO)" appearing at the top, crediting the observatories. A Spanish subtitle at the bottom reads "básicamente estamos intentando detectar RFI proveniente del espacio." (basically we are trying to detect RFI coming from space.). This transitions to a view of a different, intricate radio telescope against a cosmic, purple-blue sky, followed by a wide shot of several white radio telescope dishes scattered across a barren, mountainous landscape under a bright blue sky. The scene then shifts to another night view of a radio telescope, with a tall antenna featuring red lights in the background, all under a dense field of stars. During these transitions (from 0:05 to 0:12), the Spanish subtitle "Interferencias de radiofrecuencia generadas por inteligencia extraterrestre." (Radio frequency interference generated by extraterrestrial intelligence.) is displayed. From 0:12 to the end of the clip, a woman with dark hair and glasses, wearing a dark blue and white patterned shirt, is seen speaking directly to the camera. She stands in an indoor setting with several lush green plants behind her. As she speaks, she uses hand gestures to emphasize her points and maintains a pleasant, engaged expression. Her speech is subtitled in Spanish: "Creo que el primer tipo de tecnomarcador que detectaremos, como expliqué antes, serán estas señales variables de banda estrecha. Pero, lo que es más importante, debe ser una señal que se repita." (I believe the first type of technosignature we will detect, as I explained before, will be these narrowband variable signals. But, more importantly, it must be a repeating signal.).

The video opens with a woman with dark hair, wearing glasses and a dark, patterned shirt, speaking directly to the camera and using hand gestures. She is positioned indoors in what appears to be a modern building, with lush green plants behind her and a set of stairs visible in the background; a man in a maroon shirt and jeans briefly walks past her left side. Spanish subtitles are displayed at the bottom of the screen, stating: "No podemos detectarla una vez y decir “esto es una señal SETI”, porque, como dijo Carl Sagan hace años, afirmaciones extraordinarias requieren evidencia extraordinaria. Así que necesitamos ser capaces de detectar la misma señal múltiples veces en la misma región del cielo para asegurarnos de que no es otra cosa, que es información SETI real. Creo que tendremos que coordinarnos con tantos radiotelescopios como sea posible. Todos observando esa región, y si todos podemos verlo, esto permite tener mayor certeza en que la señal es verdadera." (We cannot detect it once and say "this is a SETI signal", because, as Carl Sagan said years ago, extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence. So we need to be able to detect the same signal multiple times in the same region of the sky to make sure it's not something else, that it's real SETI information. I think we will have to coordinate with as many radio telescopes as possible. Everyone observing that region, and if we can all see it, this allows for greater certainty that the signal is true.) The scene then transitions to a dark screen featuring white text that asks, "¿Qué implicaría para la humanidad encontrar inteligencia extraterrestre?" (What would it imply for humanity to find extraterrestrial intelligence?), with three small green pulsing dots below the question.

A young East Asian woman with dark hair and glasses, wearing a dark patterned button-up shirt, is shown from the chest up, smiling and speaking. She is positioned indoors with several large green potted plants behind her, including a tall palm-like plant on the left and a leafy bush directly behind her. The background suggests a modern interior with light-colored walls and possibly a staircase on the far right. White Spanish subtitles appear at the bottom of the screen, stating, "Creo que detectar tecnomarcadores será uno de los mayores descubrimientos científicos de nuestro tiempo. Creo que cambiará por completo nuestra perspectiva como humanos." (English: "I believe that detecting technomarkers will be one of the greatest scientific discoveries of our time. I believe it will completely change our perspective as humans.")

The video segment opens with a woman, wearing black-rimmed glasses and a dark blue patterned shirt, speaking directly to the camera. She has her dark hair pulled back and is positioned in an indoor setting featuring lush green plants, including a large potted plant to her left and a smaller leafy tree behind her. A blurred background reveals a modern building interior with a staircase. As she speaks, Spanish subtitles appear at the bottom of the screen: "Durante muchísimo tiempo, hemos pensado que somos la única vida en el universo, e, incluso dentro de la Tierra, los humanos nos vemos a nosotros mismos como la forma de vida más avanzada de todas. Si detectamos inteligencia extraterrestre, lo más probable es que sean más avanzados que nosotros. ¿Y esto qué significa? Creo que estudiar el destino de la inteligencia extraterrestre nos enseñará mucho sobre nuestro pasado, y lo más importante, nuestro futuro. Lo que tenemos delante." (For a very long time, we have thought that we are the only life in the universe, and, even within Earth, humans see ourselves as the most advanced life form of all. If we detect extraterrestrial intelligence, it is most probable that they are more advanced than us. And what does this mean? I believe that studying the destiny of extraterrestrial intelligence will teach us a lot about our past, and most importantly, our future. What lies ahead of us.). At 0:35, the scene transitions to a black screen with white text, "Inversión en SETI" (Investment in SETI), displayed centrally. Below the text, three small green dots pulse rhythmically, as the background gradually shifts to a dark greenish-blue color.

A woman with dark hair and black-rimmed glasses, wearing a dark blue and white patterned shirt, speaks directly to the camera while smiling and gesturing with her hands. She is positioned indoors, with a bright, lush green plant to her left and a smaller leafy plant behind her, against a light-colored wall and what appears to be a staircase on the right. Below her, white text with a black outline is displayed: "Alguna gente dice que es un desperdicio de dinero buscar inteligencia extraterrestre." (Some people say it's a waste of money to look for extraterrestrial intelligence.) This text introduces the topic of her discussion, which is the search for extraterrestrial intelligence.

A woman with dark hair, wearing black-framed glasses and a patterned blue and white shirt, speaks directly to the camera, gesturing with her hands. She is in an indoor setting with lush green plants behind her, and a staircase is visible in the right background. Spanish subtitles appear at the bottom of the screen, stating: "Creo que lo que están insinuando es que no creen que podamos detectar ninguna señal en un futuro cercano. Y quizá no estoy en desacuerdo. De hecho, solo hemos buscado señales SETI en una fracción diminuta del cielo. Así que es posible que haya algo ahí fuera, pero simplemente no hemos tenido los recursos para buscar de forma adecuada. Y creo que, con nuestra tecnología actual, todavía no tenemos la sensibilidad para detectar estas señales de otro planeta que puede ser que estén o no estén dirigidas hacia la Tierra. Pero si no empezamos a buscar, sí que no la encontraremos nunca." (I think what they are implying is that they don't believe we can detect any signal in the near future. And perhaps I don't disagree. In fact, we have only searched for SETI signals in a tiny fraction of the sky. So it's possible there's something out there, but we simply haven't had the resources to search properly. And I think that, with our current technology, we still don't have the sensitivity to detect these signals from another planet that may or may not be directed towards Earth. But if we don't start looking, we will never find it.) The scene then transitions to a black screen displaying white logos: "IAA" (Instituto de Astrofísica de Andalucía), "EXCELENCIA SEVERO OCHOA," and "CSIC" (Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas), accompanied by a green loading bar at the top and a white line animating across the bottom of the screen.
